what: QA's focused source review of the released subscription ASK at 3e4b406 (read at team/qa 3002218; the app tree and the connector are unchanged from the release). Three readers, one skeptic each. Offline only: no Windows process, no codex, no real connector run, no product state or credential read. 'confirmed' = the skeptic could not refute it from the lines or an offline run with the project's own test fakes. Texts are the reviewers' own, in full.

signin-secrecy.covered:
Read in full at HEAD 3002218 (Windows app tree and connector stated unchanged since 3e4b406):
- docs/adr/0003-managed-subscription-ask.md
- apps/windows/src/main/subscription.ts, src/shared/subscription-ask.ts, both preloads
- the ASK and IPC parts of src/main/main.ts, and the subscription part of src/renderer/control.ts and control.html
- services/worker/connectors/chatgpt_local.py, chatgpt_rpc.py, chatgpt_launch.py, chatgpt_receipts.py
- the sign-in, account and launch tests, and docs/verification/web/windows-subscription-ask.md for the stated design

Run, all offline on Linux (no Windows process, no codex, no real connector program, no credential or state folder opened):
- pytest on the four test_chatgpt_*.py files: 319 passed
- `node --test` on tests/subscription.test.ts: 24 passed; tests/app-ask.test.ts: 31 passed
- scratch probes under /tmp/qa-sub-source-review/signin-secrecy/: url.mjs, pyurl.py, sub.mts, more.mts, fatal.py, dead.mts, d2.mts. They use the app's own modules with the tests' fake connector, and the released bridge and client over the unit tests' fake child or a stubbed RPC.

Not established from this source:
- what the real Codex does: whether it opens a browser itself, whether it sends account/updated after a completed login, the mode of its auth.json, how it treats a second login while one is pending
- how Electron's shell.openExternal hands the address to Windows

- anything on the real display

Looked at and not reported: a `connection/login/start` reply that arrives after the app's 30 s wait is dropped and its sign-in left pending in the connector. The released connector answers or fails within its own 15 s bound, so this needs a stalled pipe.

Repository: I wrote nothing in it. `git status` showed docs/verification/qa/p0-13-subscription-ask-plan.md modified and a new p0-13-subscription-ask-windows-3e4b406.md appear during this session; those are another session's changes.

findings.title: Once the connector's Codex child ends on a fatal failure, the connector stays up refusing everything and the app never replaces it: Check and Sign in cannot recover, and 'Signed in' stays on screen
findings.evidence:
I tried to refute this and could not: the lines and two offline runs make it real.

Connector lines (services/worker/connectors/chatgpt_rpc.py):
- :277-290 `_fail` keeps the first code in `self._fatal` and kills the Codex child.
- :449-451 `_ready` raises `RPCError(self._fatal or "closed")`; it is the first call in `connection_read` (:534), `login_start` (:561) and `ask` (:611).
- :725-726 the ask's `finally` closes the client after a fatal.
- Triggers: :417-421 (any `error` notification on the active thread), :266-269 (any inner RPC over `rpc_timeout`, 15 s by default, including during a Check), :357-358 (account change mid-question), :753-755 (interrupt not confirmed in 3 s), :296-298 (child EOF).
- chatgpt_local.py:396-405 `run_stream` ends only on EOF or an unparseable line; :521-527 `_main` waits only for that or a pipe failure. Nothing ends the process when the client is dead.

App lines (apps/windows/src/main/subscription.ts):
- :148 reuses any child that is not `gone`; `gone` is set only by exit (:166-175) or `fence` (:201-206, called only for an over-long line or quit).
- :301-305 a refused read becomes `unavailable` and leaves the child in place.
- :445-449 only `unauthenticated` changes the state after a refused ask.

Run 1, /tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-signin-secrecy/fatal.py (released `run_stream` + `SubscriptionBridge` + `ChatGPTAppServer` over the unit tests' fake child):
- `[retry_error] read OK, ask quota, read quota, ask quota, login/start quota, read quota | stream still running=True fatal='quota_exhausted' closed=True codex_child_exit=-9 turn/start sent=1`
- `[auth_changed_null]` every later request `unauthenticated`.
- `[start_error]` (turn/start answered with an RPC error) every later request `failed`.
- `[init_hang]` (Codex never answers initialize) every request `unavailable`, connector still running.
- Control `[failed]` (turn/completed status failed with no `error` notification) is not fatal: the next read is OK and a second turn/start is sent. Whether the real Codex always sends an `error` notification before a failed turn cannot be settled offline; the timeout, RPC-error, crash and unconfirmed-interrupt triggers do not depend on it.

Run 2, /tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-signin-secrecy/app.mts (released `Subscription` over an in-process fake answering as above): `connectors started: 1` in every case.
- `failed`: window stays "Signed in with ChatGPT (plus)…"; the second ask is refused "ChatGPT did not complete an answer"; each Check gives "Not available. … ChatGPT did not complete an answer."
- `unauthenticated`: window says "Not signed in. Sign in with ChatGPT opens the official sign-in page…" with the Sign in button shown; pressing it gives "The sign-in did not complete. ChatGPT is not signed in (sign in from the control window)." and opens nothing. The user is told to sign in and cannot, until the app is restarted.

Corrections to the finding:
- The reviewer's `start_hang` row is a turn/start hang, not a Codex start failure. The start-failure case gives `unavailable`, not `failed`; the dead end is the same.
- docs/verification/web/windows-subscription-ask.md:106-107 says a lost connector is replaced by the user's Check or Sign in, so this is not intended behaviour.

Severity stays defect, not a blocker: it fails closed. Nothing is sent again and no credential is exposed. For the real turn, restart the app after any failed, timed-out or unconfirmed-cancel attempt. A later refused ask can be told apart in its receipt: `submission: not_submitted` with `turn_start_count` unchanged (run fatal2.py: `('req-4','not_submitted','failed',1)`, and `'uncertain'` as outcome after an `outcome_unknown` fatal).

Tests: none sends a request after a fatal (no test reads `_fatal` or calls `connection_read` after a failed ask). `test_sent_rpc_error_cleanup_does_not_claim_user_cancellation` and `test_refusals_never_publish_or_retry` only assert the code and that the child is reaped. Ran test_chatgpt_rpc.py + test_chatgpt_receipts.py (127 passed), test_chatgpt_local.py without the two tests that run the module as a program (60 passed), subscription.test.ts (24 passed).
findings.fix:
Either side is enough; both is better.
- Connector: end the process once the client is fatally closed, after the pending error line is written (for example, have `_main` also wait on a client-closed signal, or have `run_stream` stop when `client._fatal`/`_closed` is set and no task is pending). The app then sees it lost and the user's next Check starts a fresh one.
- App: in `check()`, when the read is refused with a code (subscription.ts:301-305), fence that child so the next Check starts another.
Add a connector test that sends `connection/read` after a fatal ask, and an app test for a live connector that refuses a read.

findings.title: A failed Check or sign-in start is described with the question's texts: "ChatGPT did not complete an answer", "another question is still being answered"
findings.evidence:
Confirmed by the lines and by a run; low priority.

Lines:
- apps/windows/src/main/subscription.ts:304 (read) and :344 (sign-in start) both use `ERROR_TEXT[r.code]`.
- apps/windows/src/shared/subscription-ask.ts:149 `busy: 'another question is still being answered'`, :157 `failed: 'ChatGPT did not complete an answer'`.
- services/worker/connectors/chatgpt_local.py:43-46 maps `request_failed`, `login_failed` and `timeout` to `failed`; :179-180 login/start is `busy` while a login or an ask is held.
- apps/windows/src/renderer/control.ts:380,384 prefixes "The sign-in did not complete."

Run (/tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-signin-secrecy/app.mts, released `Subscription`, fake connector):
- login/start -> failed: "Not signed in. … The sign-in did not complete. ChatGPT did not complete an answer." opened 0
- login/start -> busy: "… The sign-in did not complete. Another question is still being answered."
- connection/read -> failed: "Not available. ChatGPT did not complete an answer."

Reachability:
- `failed` is reachable without odd timing: Codex refusing or timing out `account/login/start`, `account/read` or `model/list`, or the connector refusing the address. After the first finding's fatal state it appears on every Check.
- The reviewer's `busy` example (Sign in pressed before the previous Cancel is processed) needs the second press to land before a local Codex cancel round trip finishes, so it is unlikely by hand. `busy` is deterministic in the forgotten-login state of the third finding, where it shows on an Ask.

Not a contract breach: the ADR only requires fixed texts per closed code, and that holds. The harm is a false statement that a question was attempted. A reader can tell from receipts, which are written only for asks.

Tests: none asserts the text for an error reply to `connection/login/start` or `connection/read`. subscription.test.ts:171-175 covers only a failed completion event, where detail is null. Ran subscription.test.ts: 24 passed.
findings.fix: Give Check and sign-in start their own fixed text per closed code (for example "the account could not be read", "the sign-in could not be started", "a sign-in is already pending"), and assert them in subscription.test.ts.

findings.title: The app forgets a pending sign-in without the connector's word: Cancel's answer is never read, and a signed-in read clears the sign-in without cancelling it
findings.evidence:
The mechanics are confirmed for both parts. Part 2 is a small product defect, so I raised the severity from gap_in_tests. Part 1's lasting effect is not proven.

Part 2 (sign-in cleared without a cancel): confirmed.
- apps/windows/src/main/subscription.ts:314-317 sets login to `none` and `loginId` to null on a signed_in read and sends no `connection/login/cancel`.
- apps/windows/src/renderer/control.ts:385,392 offers Sign in in state `unknown`; :393 shows Cancel only while `waiting`.
- services/worker/connectors/chatgpt_local.py:232-233 refuses `ask/start` as `busy` while `login_id` is held; :179-180 does the same for a new login/start.
- Run fatal.py `[success]`: read OK, login/start OK, ask/start busy, login/start busy.
- Run app.mts: state "The sign-in state is not known." with Sign in shown; after Sign in, "Waiting…" with Cancel shown; after Check, "Signed in with ChatGPT (plus)…" with no Cancel; requests were `connection/read, connection/login/start, connection/read`; the Ask is refused `busy` ("another question is still being answered"); `cancelLogin` then sends 0 cancels.
- Reaching it needs the account to read as signed in while this login never completes. That means state `unknown` first: either four account changes during reads (whose own text says "check again", :318) or a non-chatgpt observed mode in the connector (chatgpt_rpc.py:459-460). Rare. It ends when the browser sign-in is finished or the app is restarted.

Part 1 (Cancel pressed as the sign-in completes): the transient wrong state is confirmed; whether it lasts is unproven.
- subscription.ts:373-377 forgets the id and says `cancelled` before sending; the reply is unused. :382 then drops the connector's `completed {success:true}`.
- Run app.mts: "Not signed in. … The sign-in was cancelled." with reads: 1, although the fake's account is signed in. After a `connection/changed` it reads again and shows "Signed in…".
- So it corrects itself if the real Codex sends `account/updated` after a completed login. The repository shows only the schema (docs/verification/support/codex-app-server-0.158.0-compatibility.md:75); no login was run. One real sign-in with the notification order recorded would settle it.

Related, same root: chatgpt_rpc.py:336-338 ignores a completion whose `loginId` is not a string, and the schema allows null. If the real Codex ever sent that for the browser login, the connector would hold the login and refuse every Ask as `busy`. The same real sign-in observation settles this.

Not a blocker: the normal path (Check, Sign in, finish in browser, completion event, re-read) is covered and passes.

Tests: subscription.test.ts:180-182 covers only a cancel answered `{}`. Nothing covers a refused cancel, a completion racing a cancel, or a Check during a pending sign-in. Ran: 24 passed.
findings.fix:
- In `check()`: when a read says signed_in while a sign-in is `waiting`, send `connection/login/cancel` for it (or keep it pending and keep the Cancel button) instead of only forgetting it.
- In `cancelLogin()`: read the reply and re-read the account when it is not `{}`; or simply re-read after every cancel.
- Add tests for both, and one for a completion event that arrives after the cancel was sent.

findings.title: Connector side: a sign-in the connector itself refuses is left pending in Codex, and its address check accepts addresses a browser resolves to another host (the Windows app refuses those)
findings.evidence:
Confirmed as written, with one correction. Note is the right severity.

(a) Refused login left pending.
- services/worker/connectors/chatgpt_rpc.py:566-577: `account/login/start` is sent first, then `type`, `loginId` and `authUrl` are checked; each refusal raises `login_failed`. `self._login_id` is set only at :578 and no `account/login/cancel` is sent.
- The bridge then answers `failed` and keeps no id (chatgpt_local.py:326-332), so neither side can cancel that login.
- Run /tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-signin-secrecy/url.py (released `login_start`, stubbed `_rpc`, no child): `'https://auth.openai.com:8443/x' => refused:login_failed ['account/login/start'] kept login id: None`.

(b) Address check.
- Same run, Python 3.14.4: ACCEPTED for `https://evil.example\.openai.com/x`, `https://evil.example%2f.openai.com/x`, `…%23.openai.com/x` and `https://evil.example .openai.com/x`.
- Correction: only the backslash form resolves to another host under browser rules (WHATWG host `evil.example`). The `%2f`, `%23` and space forms are invalid URLs there, not other hosts.
- The app refuses all four (run url.mts on `officialLoginUrl`), so nothing is opened on Windows. The connector returns the raw string (:585) and the app opens only its own normalized form (apps/windows/src/shared/subscription-ask.ts:116).

Reachability: both parts need the hash-pinned Codex to return something other than its `https://auth.openai.com/…` address. The ADR puts the opening check on the desktop (docs/adr/0003-managed-subscription-ask.md:109-110). I did not check whether the macOS client has its own check; that matters before it relies on this bridge.

Tests: `test_bad_login_url_never_reaches_the_browser_seam` (test_chatgpt_rpc.py:480-491) covers one look-alike suffix and does not look at a cancel. Ran: passed.
findings.fix: On a refusal after Codex answered, send `account/login/cancel` for the returned `loginId` before raising. Reject a backslash, percent sign or whitespace in the authority (or parse with WHATWG rules), and add those cases to the test.

holds.property: 1. A sign-in is started, and a browser opened, only by the user's press of Sign in with ChatGPT.
holds.shown_by:
`login()` is called only from `lc:sub-login`, taken only from the control window (main.ts:1184, 1193). `connection/login/start` is sent only at subscription.ts:335 and `openExternal` only at :362, both inside `login()`, at most once per call (guard at :330). Connector events lead only to `check()`, which sends reads (:224-226, :388). `quit()` only fences. In the connector, `login_start` is reached only from the `connection/login/start` request (chatgpt_local.py:175-182, 326).

Tests, all run and passing: subscription.test.ts `the sign-in: its page is opened only on the user's press…`, `a change, or a completed sign-in, said while the account is being read…` (asserts no sign-in was started by it), `a sign-in that completes in the same chunk as its start's answer…`, `a sign-in whose start was answered by a connector that is then fenced…`; app-ask.test.ts `the control window: check, sign in and model are the user's presses…` and `every new request is taken only from its own window`.

Scratch run: five unsolicited `connection/login/completed` events, a `connection/login/start` event and a `connection/changed` opened nothing and sent only reads.

Caveat: the main process does not require a Check first. A sign-in press (the IPC) in `not_checked` starts a connector and opens the page; only the page hides the button (control.ts:392). docs/verification/web/windows-subscription-ask.md:106-107 documents this as intended. Whether Codex itself ever opens a browser is not visible in this repository.

holds.property: 2. The app opens only https addresses on openai.com / chatgpt.com or a subdomain, default port, no userinfo; a refused address is cancelled and said as refused; a connector cannot make it open another site, a file or custom scheme, or localhost.
holds.shown_by:
subscription-ask.ts:107-117 `officialLoginUrl`; the normalized `u.toString()` is what gets opened, not the raw string. subscription.ts:347-353: a refused address sends `connection/login/cancel` to the running child and sets `refused_address` with a fixed detail; the cancel's answer is not read.

Tests run and passing: subscription.test.ts `a sign-in address is opened only if it is https…` and the refused-address step of `the sign-in: …`.

Scratch run of about 60 inputs (`url.mjs`):
- Refused: http, file, javascript, data, blob, ms-settings, wss, ftp, view-source; localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]; port 8443; any userinfo; trailing-dot hosts; `openai.com.evil.example`; `notopenai.com`; Cyrillic look-alike and its punycode; backslash and percent-encoded tricks that move the host; inputs over 4096 characters; non-strings.
- Accepted, all resolving to a real openai.com / chatgpt.com host: upper case, explicit `:443` or empty port, empty userinfo (`https://@openai.com`), surrounding or embedded whitespace (stripped by the parser), fullwidth and soft-hyphen forms that map to `openai.com`, `https://openai.com\@evil.example/x` (opened as `https://openai.com/@evil.example/x`), any subdomain including `localhost.openai.com`, and odd labels such as `evil.example;.openai.com` (still under openai.com's zone).

The length bound is on the input only; a 4,019-character non-ASCII path was opened as 24,019 characters. The user sees: "The sign-in was not started. The sign-in address the connector gave is not an official ChatGPT address, so it was not opened." How Electron's `shell.openExternal` hands the string to Windows was not examined.

holds.property: 3. The address, login id, e-mail, tokens and credentials do not reach the renderer, logs, files the app writes, the connector's output beyond its one reply, receipts, or error messages.
holds.shown_by:
App: `status()` carries only mode, state, plan, rate_limits, models, model, login, detail, asking (subscription.ts:139-141); details are fixed strings. No `console.*` or process output anywhere in apps/windows/src (grep). The child's stderr is `ignore` (:158). `subscriptionStatus` is used only for control-window IPC and the model name in an ask record (main.ts:856, 1191, 1328); the `openExternal` error is discarded (:363). The page uses `textContent` only (control.ts:384-408).

Connector: `_account` reads only `type` and `planType`, and the plan must be in a fixed set else `unknown` (chatgpt_rpc.py:453-463); the e-mail is never read. A login completion's error is replaced by fixed codes (:339-340; chatgpt_local.py:362-364). Envelope messages are fixed (chatgpt_local.py:27-38, 131-133). No print or logging in the connector modules (grep); Codex's stderr goes to DEVNULL (chatgpt_rpc.py:145). Receipts are written only for asks, with a closed field set (chatgpt_receipts.py:22-27, 68-101); nothing is written when a login starts, completes, fails or is cancelled.

Tests run and passing: test_chatgpt_rpc.py `test_account_catalog_quota_are_exact_and_redacted` (fake returns an e-mail, account id and credits; exact result; empty stdout/stderr), `test_login_ownership_completion_race_and_cancellation`; test_chatgpt_local.py `test_login_completion_is_owned_sanitized_and_forwarded_once`, `test_connection_read_preserves_frozen_safe_account_quota_catalog_result`; test_chatgpt_receipts.py (all); subscription.test.ts `the account as read…` and the `auth.openai.com` assertions.

Scratch run: no notified status contained the address, the login id or a raw completion error.

Caveat: the app forwards whatever `plan` string the connector gives, up to 40 characters (subscription-ask.ts:103); only the connector restricts it to known plan names. What Codex writes inside its own state folder is not visible here.

holds.property: 4. Codex state is the product's own private folder, never ~/.codex; credentials are stored in it by Codex; nothing copies auth; other auth modes are not accepted as this mode.
holds.shown_by:
chatgpt_launch.py:
- :324 `CODEX_HOME = state`; :197-207 state is `LC_SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_DIR` or `<local data>/LearningCompanion/managed-chatgpt`.
- :248-259 only an empty folder is claimed (0700, marker 0600); :210-225 an unmarked, non-private, symlinked or config-bearing folder is refused.
- :311-325 minimal child environment; API keys, `CODEX_*` and provider variables are dropped.
- :67 `forced_login_method: chatgpt`, `cli_auth_credentials_store: file`, verified in the effective config at start and before each thread (:99-179).
- No code opens or copies auth.json; `shutil` is used only for `which`.

App: only the two trusted settings cross into WSL (subscription.ts:151-154).

Other modes: an account that is not `chatgpt` is reported as state `unknown`, mode null, plan null (chatgpt_rpc.py:459-460, 552-554). The window says "The sign-in state is not known." and offers Sign in; it gives no reason. A question is refused `unauthenticated` (:636-638). The app additionally treats signed_in with another mode as signed out and refuses an answer whose `auth_mode` is not chatgpt (subscription-ask.ts:87, 139).

Tests run and passing (test_chatgpt_launch.py, 319 connector tests in total): `test_managed_auth_is_never_opened_and_survives_reopen`, `test_private_environment_preserves_home_and_drops_agent_and_provider_inputs`, `test_default_uses_product_local_data_and_installed_path_without_adopting_codex_home`, `test_unmarked_nonempty_state_is_not_adopted_or_changed`, `test_state_symlinks_are_rejected_without_following_contents`, `test_command_has_complete_measured_flags_and_managed_zero_retry_provider`; test_chatgpt_rpc.py `test_non_managed_auth_stays_unsigned`; subscription.test.ts `nothing is started until the user checks; the launch is exact…`.

Not checked by product code: the mode of auth.json itself (Codex writes it), and that `initialize`'s `codexHome` equals the state folder (bound only indirectly through the config-file and skill paths).

holds.property: 5. On connection/changed the app re-reads and says what the read says; after the connector process is lost no signed-in state is shown or used.
holds.shown_by:
subscription.ts:226 `connection/changed` triggers `check()` (reads only, at most four in a row, then "not known … check again", :288-318). `lost()` turns any checked state into `unavailable` and fails a pending sign-in (:233-247). An answer from a connector that was then lost is not published (:294-300, :338). `notAskable` requires `signed_in` (:401), so an Ask never starts a new connector; `unauthenticated` from a live connector becomes signed out (:445-449).

Tests run and passing: subscription.test.ts `an account read belongs to the connector it went to…`, `a change, or a completed sign-in, said while the account is being read…`, `a question refused as not signed in by a connector that is fenced in the same chunk…`.

Scratch run: after the fake exits the state is `unavailable`, an Ask is refused, and no second connector is started. Plan and models stay in the status object but the page shows them only when signed in.

Limits: a different ChatGPT account on the same plan looks identical, because no account identity is kept (by the ADR). The case where the connector process lives but its Codex child is dead is the first finding.

signin-secrecy.holds_spot_check:
Spot-checked holds 3 and 2. Both hold; hold 3 has two small imprecisions that are not leaks.

**Hold 3 (address, login id, e-mail, tokens do not reach the renderer, logs, files, receipts or error messages): holds.**
- `status()` (apps/windows/src/main/subscription.ts:139-141) carries no login id or address. Every `detail` assignment (:243, :298, :304, :318, :344, :352, :365) is a fixed string or `ERROR_TEXT[code]`, and the code is limited to `ERROR_TEXT`'s own keys at :221; the connector's `message` is never read.
- Grep over apps/windows/src (preload and renderer included) finds no `console.` or process output. The only append is the retention manifest (main.ts:485).
- The connector's stderr is `ignore` (:158), asserted at subscription.test.ts:146. The `openExternal` error is discarded (:363). The address is used only at :347 and :362.
- Connector: `_account` reads only `type` and `planType`, and the plan must be in `_PLANS` (chatgpt_rpc.py:453-463). Completion errors become fixed codes (:339-340; chatgpt_local.py:362-364). There is no print or logging in the connector modules. Codex's stderr goes to DEVNULL (:145).
- Receipts have a closed field set (chatgpt_receipts.py:22-27, 68-101) and are written only from `begin_request`, which only `_start_ask` calls. My run fatal2.py shows no receipt for the login and read scenarios.
- Tests run and passing: `test_account_catalog_quota_are_exact_and_redacted` (the fake returns an e-mail, an account id and credits; exact result; empty stdout and stderr), `test_login_ownership_completion_race_and_cancellation`, `test_login_completion_is_owned_sanitized_and_forwarded_once`, test_chatgpt_receipts.py, and subscription.test.ts:164 (status contains no `auth.openai.com`) and :72 (e-mail and token dropped by `readAccount`).
- Imprecision 1: the login id also crosses the private pipe in each `connection/login/completed` event (chatgpt_local.py:362-366), not only in the start's reply. That is the ADR's shape, and the app does not forward it.
- Imprecision 2: `subscriptionStatus` is also read at main.ts:1231, as a boolean to the overlay.

**Hold 2 (only https on openai.com / chatgpt.com or a subdomain, default port, no userinfo; a refused address is cancelled and said as refused): holds.**
- Lines: apps/windows/src/shared/subscription-ask.ts:107-117; the normalized `u.toString()` is what is opened. subscription.ts:347-353 sends `connection/login/cancel` to the running child, sets `refused_address` with a fixed detail and returns before `openExternal`.
- Tests run and passing: subscription.test.ts:76-81 (`a sign-in address is opened only if it is https…`) and :183-187 (refused-address step).

findings.title: After any failed turn or refusal the connector stays alive but permanently dead; the app never starts a new one
findings.evidence:
Could not refute. The cited lines say what the finding claims: services/worker/connectors/chatgpt_rpc.py:277-290 (_fail sets _fatal once and kills the child), 417-421 (any on-thread `error` notification calls _fail, whatever willRetry is), 449-451 (_ready raises the stale _fatal for connection_read, login_start, login_cancel and ask), 724-726 (ask closes the client when _fatal is set). chatgpt_local.py:391-412 (run_stream keeps reading lines; nothing ends it or recreates the client) and 510-527 (_main waits only for the stream end or a pipe failure). apps/windows/src/main/subscription.ts:147-148 (start() returns the live child), 249-251, 282, 335, 422; the only ways the app drops a child are fence() for an over-long line, the child's own exit, and quit (201-206, 233-247, 475-479). apps/windows/src/main/main.ts has no restart path (the only calls are check, login, cancelLogin, chooseModel, ask, cancel, stopSession, quit).

I reproduced it independently through run_stream itself (scratch: /tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-isolation/probe.py; product ChatGPTAppServer + run_stream + the unit tests' fake python child; no Codex, no network). After `error` then turn/completed failed: first ask -> `failed`, inner child rc -9, client closed, fatal incomplete_turn; run_stream still running; second ask -> `failed` with zero new inner requests, receipt submission=not_submitted outcome=failed turn_start_count=1; later connection/read -> `failed`; later connection/login/start -> `failed`. With codexErrorInfo `unauthorized`: every later request, including connection/login/start, -> `unauthenticated` with no inner request. Same dead state after model/rerouted and after item/tool/requestUserInput. Control: turn/completed failed with no preceding `error` notification leaves the client usable (second ask sends a real second turn/start, login/start works).

Two limits on the finding's wording. (1) That a real failed turn always takes the fatal path depends on the real `error` notification carrying the active threadId: line 381 drops notifications without it, and my control with an `error` that has no threadId gave no fatal. Support's receipt (docs/verification/support/codex-app-server-isolated-no-retry.json) records the order `error`, `turn/completed` but not the params' keys; the unit-test fake assumes threadId/turnId. The dead state itself does not depend on this: server requests, reroute, a 15 s RPC timeout, an unconfirmed interrupt, the child's own exit (298) and the event cap reach it by the lines alone. (2) A failed start() has the same effect (chatgpt_rpc.py:157-159 plus chatgpt_local.py:143-145: every later request gets `unavailable`), which the finding does not list.

Severity stays defect, not a blocker: everything fails closed and nothing is sent a second time. Consequence for the real-turn run stands: a second Ask after a failed, refused or unconfirmed-cancel turn is answered `failed` instantly with nothing sent (only the receipt's not_submitted shows that), so quit and restart the app between real calls. Tests: no test at rpc, bridge or app level sends a second request after a fatal (read test_chatgpt_rpc.py, test_chatgpt_local.py, apps/windows/tests/subscription.test.ts test list). I ran the four connector test files plus tests/evals/test_subscription_ask.py offline: 431 passed, 2 deselected (the test that runs the connector module as a program was not run).
findings.fix: Make the connector end itself when its client is fatally closed, so the app's existing `lost` path (subscription.ts:233-247) starts a fresh connector on the next user press; or recreate the client inside run_stream. Separately, do not treat an `error` notification with willRetry=false as fatal: let turn/completed failed map it (chatgpt_rpc.py:695-702 already does, without a fatal). Add a bridge test that sends a second ask, a connection/read and a login/start after each fatal mode.

findings.title: Per-turn event cap counts streamed deltas, so answers well inside the 32,000-character limit are killed
findings.evidence:
Could not refute the mechanism. services/worker/connectors/chatgpt_rpc.py:383-385 increments active['events'] for every notification on the active thread before any method branch (386-421), and raises protocol_error past MAX_TURN_EVENTS = 4096 (line 25); 326-327 turns that into _fail('protocol_error'), which kills the child; chatgpt_local.py:50-51 maps protocol_error to public `unavailable`. `item/agentMessage/delta` is not caught earlier: it matches neither the tool prefixes at 363-364 nor the item/started|completed check at 372. The connector does not opt out of delta notifications at initialize (147-149), and the schema audit for this binary lists `item/agentMessage/delta` among its notification methods (docs/verification/support/codex-app-server-0.158.0-schema-audit.json, notification_methods).

My own run (same scratch probe, tests' fake child): 4,090, 4,094 and 4,095 on-thread deltas followed by a normal completion -> answered (12,270 to 12,285 chars); 4,096, 4,100 and 9,000 deltas -> RPCError protocol_error, child rc -9. The exact edge is the 4,097th on-thread notification, counting turn/completed itself, and turn/started, item/started, item/completed and thread/status/changed all draw on the same budget. 9,000 deltas on another thread id -> answered, so only on-thread notifications count. The 9,000-delta case is a 27,000-character answer, inside ADR 0003's 32,000-character limit (docs/adr/0003-managed-subscription-ask.md:52-53). After the kill the connector is dead as in the first finding, and the user is told the connection is unavailable although a turn was acknowledged.

Not settled offline: how many delta notifications the real binary emits per answer. Nothing in the repository measures it (Support's synthetic turn recorded no delta; rpc_methods in codex-app-server-isolated-no-retry.json). A short acceptance answer is unlikely to reach the cap; a long full_solution answer or one with a long streamed reasoning summary plausibly does. What would settle it: count on-thread notifications in one real turn, or a loopback run whose synthetic SSE reply streams several thousand text deltas. Test coverage: none; grep for `delta` and MAX_TURN_EVENTS in services/worker/connectors/tests returns nothing (ran the grep).
findings.fix: Count only the notifications the connector acts on (turn/started, turn/completed, item/started, item/completed), or opt out of delta notifications at initialize if 0.158.0 supports it; keep a separate generous bound on ignored notifications. Add a fake-child test with several thousand deltas followed by a normal completion. For the real-turn run, keep the question to one that needs a short answer.

findings.title: The prompt invites a clarification while the only tool still advertised is the clarification tool, and a use of it leaves no trace
findings.evidence:
The text and code facts are as cited. services/learning/subscription_ask.py:147 says 'Do not act in apps, submit answers, run commands, fetch links, or use tools.' and 151 says 'ask a small clarification if needed'. docs/verification/support/codex-app-server-isolation-followup.md:7 and 137-141 record request_user_input as the one tool still advertised, for the synthetic model only. chatgpt_rpc.py:304-311 answers any server request with -32601 and kills the child, recording nothing first; chatgpt_receipts.py:22-27 has no reason field. My receipt dump (scratch: /tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-isolation/probe_receipts.py) for user_input_request and server_request: public `failed`, submission=acknowledged, terminal_status=null, outcome=failed, produced_item_types=[], actual_model unchanged; the two are identical.

The trigger is not shown and cannot be shown offline: whether a real model calls the tool, and whether 0.158.0 then raises item/tool/requestUserInput to the client at all. One fact in the repository points against the server request: the same binary's feature table lists `default_mode_request_user_input  under development  false` (docs/verification/support/codex-app-server-0.158.0-cli-receipt.json, feature_override_output), so in the default mode the binary may answer the model's call itself instead of asking the client. If it does, the turn would continue with a second model request inside the same turn, which the receipt does not count (turn_start_count counts stdin writes of turn/start only, chatgpt_rpc.py:238-241). Support never made its synthetic model call the tool (followup.md:140-141).

One correction: the finding says the receipt is 'identical to a rerouted model'. It is not: model/rerouted writes toModel into actual_model before the kill (chatgpt_rpc.py:369; my dump shows actual_model=other-model for rerouted). It is identical to an `error`-notification failure whose turn/completed was not yet read, and to any other mid-turn fatal that maps to `failed`.

What would settle it: a loopback synthetic-provider run under the full launch configuration where the fake model emits a request_user_input function call, recording whether a server request arrives and how many HTTP requests follow. Tests cover the refusal (test_chatgpt_rpc.py::test_user_input_server_request_is_denied_and_child_killed_after_verified_start, ran, passes), not the prompt wording.
findings.fix: Reword line 151 so the clarification is asked in the text answer itself (for example 'state what is unclear in your answer'). Record the refused server-request method, from a closed list, in the receipt.

findings.title: The internal closed code is lost: tool refusal, model mismatch and a plain failed turn cannot be told apart, and the public mapping is untested
findings.evidence:
Confirmed with one correction. findings.evidence:
The configuration and evidence facts check out; the failure itself is not shown. services/worker/connectors/chatgpt_launch.py:37-44: _DISABLED has 23 names and none of unified_exec, sleep_tool, unbounded_connection_retries. 131-143: the verifier walks only the expected leaves; it does not require any other feature to be off and never sees an outbound tool list. test_chatgpt_launch.py:262 asserts features.unified_exec is not set, and :486-489 shows the verifier accepting an effective features.unified_exec = True (both ran, pass). I re-derived the enabled rows from docs/verification/support/codex-app-server-0.158.0-cli-receipt.json (feature_override_output): all fifteen names in the finding print true (unified_exec, unified_exec_tty, write_stdin_approval, sleep_tool, browser_use_external, browser_use_full_cdp_access, in_app_browser, in_app_local_automation, guardian_approval, realtime_conversation, tool_call_mcp_elicitation, auth_elicitation, worktrees, plugin_sharing, unbounded_connection_retries); apply_patch_freeform is `removed false`; unified_exec_focused_checks shows the switch has no effect. Support's tool list [request_user_input] is for model lc-support-synthetic on provider lc_probe (codex-app-server-isolated-no-retry.json, probe.requests[0].tools), and Support draws no conclusion for a real catalog model (codex-app-server-isolation-followup.md:11-12, 164-168) or for retries beyond one HTTP 503 (:92-93).

Two cautions on reading that table. It is the output of the CLI's feature listing with an earlier disable set, not the effective configuration of the product launch: enable_request_compression prints true there although the launch now disables it, and the product's effective values are read back through config/read only for the expected leaves. And a feature printing true does not show its tool is offered, as Support's own unified_exec result demonstrates.

Unproven: that a real catalog model is offered a shell, patch or other tool under this launch, and that a command would start before the kill. The backstops are in the lines (per-thread read-only sandbox with networkAccess false verified at chatgpt_rpc.py:658-664; any non-message item or server request fails the turn at 304-311, 363-377, 423-429), so if it happens the turn fails closed and no text is shown. What would settle it: the outbound tool list captured for the real model's slug (a loopback run using that slug so the binary applies its own model metadata), plus a refused-connection and a cut-stream case for the retry count. In the real turn, the receipt's produced_item_types shows whether a tool item appeared, not whether a tool was offered.
findings.fix: Keep it as a stated limit of the real-turn acceptance. If Support repeats the loopback run, use the real catalog model's slug and add a refused-connection and a cut-stream case with and without features.unbounded_connection_retries=false; add the flag to _DISABLED only if it changes the request count.

findings.title: A connector whose inner Codex client has failed stays alive and is never replaced: every later Check or Ask gets the old failure's code until the app is restarted
findings.evidence:
I could not refute it; the lines say what the finding claims, and a scratch run reproduced both halves.

Connector: chatgpt_rpc.py:277-290 (`_fail` keeps the first code in `_fatal` and kills the child), :449-451 (`_ready` raises `RPCError(self._fatal or "closed")` on every later call), :725-726 (the ask's `finally` closes the inner client when fatal). chatgpt_local.py:320-332 answers the error and carries on; :391-405 `run_stream` ends only at end of input or an unparseable line. Nothing in `_main` (:510-551) watches the inner client.

Scratch run (released bridge + released RPC client + the project's fake child, /tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-ipl/f1_f3.py), sequence read, ask, read, read, ask:
- `retry_error` (an `error` notification): quota, quota, quota, quota; inner_fatal=quota_exhausted, inner closed, child rc -9, stream not done.
- `auth_changed_null`: unauthenticated four times.
- `ignore_interrupt` (unconfirmed interrupt): failed four times.
- `start_hang` (inner RPC timeout): failed four times.

App: subscription.ts:147-148 reuses any child that is not gone; :301-305 a failed read only sets `unavailable`; :201-206 the child is ended only for an over-long line or quit. Scratch run with the project's synthetic connector (/tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-ipl/app.test.ts): three Checks answered `quota` used one connector, never exited; a second Ask after a failed Ask (state still signed_in) was written to the same connector and returned refused/quota.

Two corrections to the finding's wording:
- Not every failed turn is fatal. A turn ended by `turn/completed` with status failed and no `error` notification (fake mode `failed`), and a 120 s timeout whose interrupt is confirmed (mode `hang`), left the client usable: later reads answered normally. Whether real Codex always sends an `error` notification with a failed turn is not settled offline.
- One consequence it did not state: after an auth change mid-turn the app says signed_out and tells the user to sign in, but `connection/login/start` also goes through `_ready()` (chatgpt_rpc.py:561), so sign-in cannot start until the app is restarted.

Severity stays defect, not a blocker: the stale answers never reach ChatGPT and use no allowance, and restarting the app recovers. No existing test covers it on either side; the nearest, test_chatgpt_local.py::test_real_rpc_cleanup_does_not_report_user_cancellation (ran, passes), stops at the first error.
findings.fix: Connector: when the inner client is fatal or closed, answer the request in hand and end the stream (break out of `run_stream`), so the app sees a lost connector and the next Check starts a fresh one. Or app: end the child (`fence`) when a read is answered with an error code. Until fixed, the real-turn procedure should restart the app after any turn that did not answer, and should not read a Check after a failure as the account's state.

findings.title: The connector fails any turn with more than 4096 thread notifications, streamed deltas included, although it allows answers up to 32,000 characters
findings.evidence:
The mechanism is confirmed by lines and by a run. How often a real turn reaches it is not settled offline.

Lines: chatgpt_rpc.py:25 `MAX_TURN_EVENTS = 4096`. :378-385: any notification not returned earlier whose `threadId` is the active thread's does `active["events"] += 1`, then raises `RPCError("protocol_error")` past the bound; there is no exemption by method. :326-327 turns the raise into `_fail("protocol_error")`, which kills the child. The answer bound it cannot reach is :23 and :433-440 (32,000 characters). Support's table (docs/verification/support/codex-app-server-0.158.0-compatibility.md:80) gives `item/agentMessage/delta` a `threadId`.

Scratch run (/tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-ipl/f1_f3.py; project fake child plus one added delta scenario, through the released bridge):
- 100 and 4090 deltas: answered, and the next read was normal.
- 4100 and 8000 deltas: ask ended as error `unavailable`; inner_fatal=protocol_error, inner closed, child rc -9; the next read also `unavailable` (the stuck state of the first finding).

No existing test sends delta notifications (grep of test_chatgpt_rpc.py: no 'delta').

Not settled offline: how many notifications real Codex 0.158.0 sends per turn. If it streams about one delta per token, plus reasoning-summary deltas and token-usage updates, an answer of roughly 16,000 characters or a short answer after long reasoning would pass 4096. To settle: count the notifications of the first real turn, or have Support measure a long answer. Keep the first real turn as 'A hint'.
findings.fix: Do not count delta notifications against the event bound (bound their total bytes instead), or raise the bound to fit a 32,000-character answer plus reasoning. Add a test with more than 4096 deltas.

- event written in the same tick as the reply: 4 reads, state 'unknown', detail 'check again' (the bounded path the existing test covers);
- event written one tick after the reply (setImmediate): 25,581 reads, 51,162 status notices, state flipping checking/signed_in, one connector.

Existing test: subscription.test.ts 'a change, or a completed sign-in, said while the account is being read is read once more…' (ran, passes) emits the event from `onCall`, that is before the reply, so it exercises only the in-check bound.

If it did loop, each read costs three inner RPCs and one of the bridge's 4096 request ids (chatgpt_local.py:166-170), after which every request is refused. Defect in a stated fence, low likelihood; not a blocker.

findings.title: At the bridge's 4096-request limit a Stop or Cancel is refused without being recorded, and the in-flight question ends as 'cancelled', which the app can record as a confirmed cancel
findings.evidence:
Confirmed by lines and a run. It stays a note: reaching it needs 4096 envelope requests in one connector lifetime.

Lines: chatgpt_local.py:164-171 checks the history limit before the method is looked at; it sets `exhausted`, sets the active ask's cancelled flag, and raises. :200-210 (the stop's own handling, `stopped_sessions.add`, the interrupt) is never reached. :289-290 answers the ask as `cancelled` whenever `_cancelled(active)`, whatever the inner interrupt returned. subscription.ts:443 returns {status:'cancelled', uncertain:false} for a `cancelled` reply when the app itself did not cancel.

Scratch run (/tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-ipl/f2_f5.py, released bridge + the tests' synthetic inner client, history preset to 4095): session/stop gave `unavailable`; `stopped_sessions` stayed empty; no inner interrupt was called; the ask ended as `cancelled`; a later ask/cancel and connection/read gave `unavailable`; the bridge was not closed.

App side (/tmp/qa-sub-source-review/skeptic-ipl/app.test.ts): a `cancelled` reply to a question the app did not cancel returned {status:'cancelled', uncertain:false}.

No fence is breached: after the limit every ask/start is refused too (:166 and :228), and the app keeps its own stopped set. If the app did send Stop or Cancel, the refused receipt keeps the outcome uncertain (subscription.ts:430-433), which is right. The wrong case is only an unprompted `cancelled`, for example a Check sent as the 4097th request while a question is out.

No existing test covers the limit or an unprompted `cancelled`; subscription.test.ts 'a cancel or a Stop is a confirmed interruption only by its own exact receipt…' (ran, passes) covers only app-initiated cancels.
findings.fix: App: at subscription.ts:443 return uncertain:true for a `cancelled` reply that no own cancel or Stop receipt confirmed. Connector: handle ask/cancel and session/stop before the history limit.

findings.title: At quit or fence the connector's real end is not known and not said; the app's 5 s wait is shorter than the connector's own 8 s cleanup
findings.evidence:
The code facts hold. The consequence on the WSL side is runtime behaviour and not shown.

Lines: subscription.ts:205 calls `endChild(...)` with `end_ms ?? 5_000`; its result only joins `closing` and is never read. main.ts:1355-1362 passes no `end_ms`, so 5 s is the product value. capture-host.ts:319-347 waits, kills the shim, waits 2 s more, and returns the note 'the wsl.exe shim was ended, which does not show that the host process in WSL ended', which is discarded here. chatgpt_local.py:25-26 `SHUTDOWN_SECONDS = 8`; chatgpt_rpc.py:776-783 allows 3 s after terminate plus 3 s after kill.

A second connector started while the first still holds the lock gets `busy` at chatgpt_launch.py:263-281, and chatgpt_local.py:528-546 answers its first handshake `unavailable` and exits, so the next Check starts cleanly.

Practical weight is small: at quit no later Check exists, and a Codex child that exits on terminate keeps the connector well under 5 s. It matters only after an over-long-line fence with a Codex child that ignores terminate.

Not settled offline: whether killing wsl.exe ends the WSL-side process. To settle: the process watch in a display run after a forced fence.

Existing tests: subscription.test.ts 'a connector ended here for a line that is not the envelope's…' (ran, passes) and app-ask.test.ts 'quitting with the connector running…' (read, not run) cover the bounded wait, not what is said afterwards.
findings.fix: Keep `endChild`'s result and say 'not confirmed ended' in the status after a fence; make the default `end_ms` at least the connector's own 8 s bound.

findings.title: Nothing checks, after a turn, that the Codex child left no thread or history content in the product state on the WSL side
findings.evidence:
The 'nothing checks' half is true from the lines.

chatgpt_rpc.py:647-651 requests `"ephemeral": True`, and :663 refuses unless the reply's `thread.ephemeral is True`. :672-676 sends the picture as a data URL, so the connector writes no picture file. chatgpt_launch.py:32-36 `_FORBIDDEN` holds only config, hook, skill and plugin names. :210-221 `_check_state` refuses only those names, symlinks, a wrong marker and wrong permissions, so a sessions folder or history file would pass. A grep of services/worker/connectors/*.py for sessions/history/rollout finds no other check.

The 'did Codex write one' half cannot be settled here: opening or listing the state directory is forbidden in this review, and Codex was not run. The Backend and Support evidence I found (docs/verification/backend/p0-04-managed-subscription-launch.md:98, docs/verification/support/codex-app-server-isolation-followup.md:71) records that the thread was reported ephemeral, not what was on disk afterwards.

To settle: after the first real turn, whoever is permitted lists the entry names (names only) in the product state directory and compares with a listing from before the turn.
findings.fix: Add a names-only before/after listing of the product state directory to the real-turn procedure; if Codex is found to write thread content, add those names to the post-turn check.

findings.title: The effective bound on a real answer is the connector's 120 s, not the app's 5 minutes; a turn cut off there is recorded as 'refused' with code 'failed'
findings.evidence:
The lines say what the finding claims.

chatgpt_launch.py:340-342 builds `ChatGPTAppServer` without timeouts, so the defaults at chatgpt_rpc.py:100-101 apply: 15 s per RPC, 120 s per turn, 3 s for shutdown and interrupt. chatgpt_rpc.py:684-691: no completion within `turn_timeout` leads to `_interrupt_request`, then `RPCError("outcome_unknown")`. chatgpt_local.py:43 maps `outcome_unknown`, `uncertain` and `timeout` to public `failed`. subscription.ts:422 (300 s) is therefore never the effective bound. :450 returns {status:'refused', code:'failed'}, whose type comment at :79 says 'Known not answered'. overlay.ts:922 renders 'No answer: ChatGPT did not complete an answer. It was not sent again.'

Runs: scratch mode `hang` through the released bridge gave ask error `failed`, and later reads answered normally (the client stays usable when the interrupt is confirmed). Existing test test_chatgpt_local.py::test_real_rpc_cleanup_does_not_report_user_cancellation[hang] (ran, passes) asserts public `failed` with receipt outcome `uncertain` and one turn/start.

So in the app's record 'refused' does not mean 'not sent'; only the connector's receipt (`submission`, `outcome`) tells whether the turn was submitted and may have used the allowance. The visible text is truthful.

If the interrupt at 120 s is not confirmed within 3 s, the client goes fatal and the connector is in the stuck state of the first finding (scratch mode `ignore_interrupt`).
findings.fix: For the real turn, read the receipt, not the app record's status, to decide whether the allowance may have been used. Consider recording code `failed` as status 'uncertain' in the app, or adding a 'submitted' fact to the record.
